identity.title: Embodied Agent Interface: Benchmarking LLMs for Embodied Decision Making

problem.claim: Evaluate LLMs for embodied decision making.

gap.claim: Existing work lacks systematic performance understanding because applications differ in domains, purposes, inputs, and outputs; final success rates also obscure missing abilities and failure locations.

contributions.claim: Proposes the Embodied Agent Interface to formalize varied embodied tasks and LLM-module input-output specifications.
Unifies embodied tasks, four decision-making modules, and fine-grained error metrics covering hallucination, affordance, and planning errors.

stated_novelty.claim: The stated distinction is a generalized interface and benchmark that jointly standardize task/module specifications and decompose evaluation by error type.

narrative_sequence.summary: The paper aims to evaluate LLMs for embodied decision making.
It identifies fragmented prior applications and coarse final-success evaluation as barriers to systematic diagnosis and selective use.
It introduces a generalized interface spanning tasks, modules, and formalized input-output specifications.
The authors report that the resulting benchmark assesses subtasks and identifies strengths and weaknesses in LLM-powered embodied systems.

source_observation.claim: The abstract replaces a single final success rate with fine-grained metrics organized around error types and specific modules.

lessons.interpretation: This links evaluation outputs to actionable capability diagnoses.
lessons.application: For a modular AI benchmark, report module-level and error-type metrics alongside aggregate task success.
lessons.exception: This decomposition may be unsuitable when errors cannot be reliably assigned to distinct modules or categories.

unknowns: The abstract gives no benchmark task inventory, dataset size, metric definitions, baselines, numerical results, or validation protocol.
It does not establish that the proposed interface or benchmark improves agent performance or is novel relative to prior benchmarks.
